summary: An 8.8 magnitude earthquake hit Chile, causing significant damage; Wikinews correspondent Diego Grez, in Pichilemu, said electricity was restored last night after more than three days without radio, cellphone or TV, and that gas and water remained available in Pichilemu though nearby Bucalemu had been four days without them. He described a slow government response—saying the mayor was absent during the quake and arrived Sunday, and that they did not receive food until yesterday—and said residents evacuated to Cerro La Cruz hill where crowds, looting and unsanitary conditions occurred. Grez said most Pichilemu houses, including his, remained secure with only a broken glass, ill people were taken to a high school because of tsunami risk and then returned, and after a strong aftershock they briefly fled again but now have had no further problems.
